title: [focusgroupV2] Grid Navigation and supporting features.

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
## What problem are you trying to solve?

The initial `focusgroup` proposal provides declarative directional navigation for composite widgets, but it does not cover several related patterns that authors commonly implement with script:

* Items such as cards or messages that contain nested controls. In these cases, only the active item's controls should participate in sequential focus navigation.
* Feeds where users navigate between articles directionally while retaining access to controls within the active article.
* Two-dimensional grids that require consistent row and column navigation, wrapping, and focus memory.

Authors currently reproduce this behavior with custom focus management and mutation handling. Implementations vary across sites, resulting in inconsistent keyboard navigation and additional accessibility risk.

## What solutions exist today?

### Roving Tabindex
Authors use JavaScript to manage `tabindex`, track the active item, filter nested controls from sequential focus navigation, and calculate directional movement through grids.

Libraries and design systems provide their own implementations, but they differ in their handling of nested controls, focus restoration, writing modes, mutations, grid edges, and invalid topology.

### Spatial Navigation
From the [original focusgroup explainer](https://open-ui.org/components/scoped-focusgroup.explainer/#css-spatial-navigation):

[CSS spatial navigation](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-nav-1/) defines a general model for moving focus with arrow keys (or any other directional input mechanism) across an entire document, oriented to spatial position rather than to a specific composite widget. Focusgroup and CSS spatial navigation address different scopes and are expected to compose:

* Focusgroup governs directional navigation within author-defined composite widgets. It defines a single tab stop per segment, last-focused memory, axis restriction, and wrapping: semantics tied to a recognized interaction pattern.
* CSS spatial navigation governs directional navigation between controls across the document, providing directional traversal as an alternative or assistive means of reaching any focusable element on the page.

## How would you solve it?
1. My primary concern is with adding support for declarative, two directional focus navigation for an individual control.
2. As a secondary concern, I want to ensure that any new behavior intuitively interacts with the existing focus navigation patterns that users are already familiar with, an additional consideration is made to ensure that authors have control over how nested focusable content is entered. The focusgroup V2 proposal addresses this need by adding an additional modifier to focusgroup, allowing developers to pick the behavior they want to define how users interact with nested content. I am very open to ideas and considerations around how this works, even if this means a separate feature/proposal.

#### Extend the `focusgroup` proposal with the Focusgroup V2 additions developed in Open UI:
* A `grid` behavior for two-dimensional navigation through rectangular, spanless grids.
* Companion grid modifiers for manual row enrollment and per-axis wrapping or flow. 
* An `itemcontrols` modifier that retains eligible nested controls of the active item in sequential focus navigation and removes those associated with inactive items.
* A `feed` behavior for block-axis navigation through streams of articles with nested controls.

These additions reuse the ownership, navigation, entry, memory, nesting, opt-out, and key-conflict rules from the existing `focusgroup` proposal.

[Focusgroup V2 explainer](https://open-ui.org/components/focusgroup-v2.explainer/)

## Anything else?

This proposal builds on the existing Focusgroup work:

* [WHATWG issue #11641](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11641)
* [Draft HTML specification PR #11723](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11723)
* [Open UI Focusgroup V1 proposal](https://open-ui.org/components/scoped-focusgroup.explainer/)

This issue tracks the V2 additions separately so they can receive early standards and implementer feedback without expanding the scope of the V1 specification work.
